doc.title: Joseph Rene and Edna Kelly Interview, 1969-12-15

title: What the dance halls were like: admission, deposits, manners and wine
summary: Edna describes society balls, how bands were paid a deposit, respectable slow dancing, intermissions and Chris's wine.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Yes. Well, see if you can try and think of anything more to tell me about one of those dancers which you went to. I mean, just try and imagine that you're just trying to describe it to me because I've never been to one of those and I don't know what it is.

Well, the dance hall is big and wide and they have little benches upside the wall. All around. In the kitchen they have, in the back they have something like a room with drinks and that. And the music be up on the stand and all the lights is on and you get up and dance.
How, when would it start? What time? 9 o'clock. 9 o'clock. 9 o'clock. Go on.
9 until.
That's the way it's here. Until. Would that be just a weekend or would that be in the middle of the weekend?

No, anytime, anytime somebody want to give a ball, you see a ball, you see a ball, you see a ball, like a society want to give a ball. You know how I would call it a ball. One ball, one ball next Sunday night, one ball next Sunday night, like that. Different, different nights, you know. Yeah.
And, and the society would give the ball. Yeah.
I see.
Now would they charge you? Did you pay admission?

We paid admission at the door. But, if, my husband used to tell us how much he charged for his band. And so his man that's giving the dance, he would ask him how much deposit he had to put down, he used to put a deposit on the band, you know. Twenty dollars, thirty dollars, whatever he wanted. If the band come up to a hundred or something, you know. And then he had the deposit on the band. And on that night, that's the dance he had to go play. That's the way that's going. I see.
And then they'd stop playing and then you'd say you'd dance and so on. What way would you dance? I mean, you know, like nowadays they'd dance all different. Oh no.
They'd dance slow and nice, not only shaking and crazy. Yes. Yes.
Hold in and you'd hold your partner. Yeah, yes. I see.
Very respectable. Yes. The gentleman would hold a lady like a lady. Yes.
And you'd do sort of like fast-struck. Yeah. Yeah. And then they'd have intermissions? They'd have intermissions and things or what? Oh yeah.

They'd have to, they'd stop playing for a while. Then you'd go down, you'd go down in the back, you know, that's where the drinks were. Everybody would go drink. And the band, the band would come down, they'd go get a drink and after a while it comes.
It's all he cares. Did Chris drink much when he was on the job? Yes. Oh yes. When he was playing? Every time he got ready. What did he like?
Wine.
You like wine?
He was no fool, though. No. No. People drink wine these days, they're crazy. But he wasn't that crazy.
